pr.title: De-LLVM the unchecked shifts [MCP#693]
pr.description:
This is just one part of the MCP (https://github.com/rust-lang/compiler-team/issues/693), but it's the one that IMHO removes the most noise from the standard library code.

Seems net simpler this way, since MIR already supported heterogeneous shifts anyway, and thus it's not more work for backends than before.

r? WaffleLapkin
pr.author: scottmcm

processing.reason:
PR #123226 (MCP#693) is a refactor/optimization, not a semantic fix, so there is no source-grounded incorrect transformation to encode.

Original (pre-PR) `u16::unchecked_shl(self, rhs: u32)` inlined to: `assume(rhs <= 65535_u32); let r = rhs as u16; _0 = ShlUnchecked(self, r)`. The new lowering instead produces `_0 = ShlUnchecked(self_u16, rhs_u32)` with heterogeneous operands. For every input that is defined under the unchecked-shift contract (RHS < 16), the old cast `rhs as u16` is lossless and the old `rhs <= 65535` assume holds, so both versions compute the same shift result. For every other input (RHS >= 16, including RHS > 65535), the actual shift amount is out of range and is UB in both versions (the old assume only adds another UB condition). Hence no concrete defined input can distinguish them, and Miri would report UB for both on any candidate differing input.

The other changes (heterogeneous `unchecked_shl<T,U>`/`unchecked_shr<T,U>` signatures, direct `ShlUnchecked`/`ShrUnchecked` lowering, and the backend's `icmp ult b, 16` vs `65536` assume) are codegen/optimization differences, not value differences on defined inputs. Manufacturing a "counterexample" would require masking an unchecked shift, using an out-of-range shift amount, or an unrelated return-value change—all explicitly disallowed. Therefore no valid original/transformed pair exists.

analysis.summary: MCP#693 de-LLVM'd unchecked shifts by making `unchecked_shl`/`unchecked_shr` accept heterogeneous `<T, U>` operands. `LowerIntrinsics` now lowers both same-type and mixed-type calls directly to `ShlUnchecked`/`ShrUnchecked` with the original RHS operand, while `Inline` no longer sees the library's `conv_rhs_for_unchecked_shift!` RHS cast and narrow-type `assume`. The refactor moves range preservation from MIR/library into shift lowering: checked shifts mask the RHS, unchecked shifts do not mask but add an in-range assume (or future `trunc nuw`) when truncating a wider RHS. This is an optimization/refactor, not a confirmed bug fix.
analysis.originalLogic: Before MCP#693, `unchecked_shl`/`unchecked_shr` were homogeneous `(T,T)->T` intrinsics. The `core::num` method `unchecked_shl(self, rhs: u32)` called `conv_rhs_for_unchecked_shift!`, which for `SelfT::BITS < 32` inserted `intrinsics::assume($x <= (<$SelfT>::MAX as u32));` and then `$x as $SelfT`, so MIR reaching LowerIntrinsics/Inline already contained an `IntToInt` cast (and sometimes an `assume`) plus a same-typed shift. For wider LHS the macro still emitted `$x as $SelfT`. LowerIntrinsics then rewrote `unchecked_shl::<i32>(...)` to `ShlUnchecked`. The backend `cast_shift_expr_rhs` handled any remaining shift-type mismatch; checked `Shl`/`Shr` used `build_masked_lshift`/`build_masked_rshift`, which masked the RHS, while `ShlUnchecked`/`ShrUnchecked` only cast the RHS.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: Historical transformation replaced by this PR (a refactor, not a confirmed miscompile): normalize the shift amount to the LHS integer type at the library/MIR level before the unchecked shift. For narrow LHS the old macro emitted `assume($x <= (<$SelfT>::MAX as u32))` and then `$x as $SelfT`; for wide LHS it emitted `$x as $SelfT`. After inlining, e.g. `u16.unchecked_shl(b: u32)` became `_5 = _4 as u16 (IntToInt); _0 = ShlUnchecked(_3, move _5)` with an extra `assume(Le(_4, 65535_u32))`, instead of directly `_0 = ShlUnchecked(_3, _4)` with heterogeneous `u16`/`u32` operands. The old assume was bounded by the truncation range (`SelfT::MAX`), whereas the new assumption uses the shift-width bound (the codegen test changes from `icmp ult i32 %b, 65536` to `icmp ult i32 %b, 16`). Do not reintroduce the library-side cast/assume as a correctness fix: checked shifts must still mask the RHS, while unchecked shifts must not mask but must preserve the in-range fact when a wider RHS is truncated.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust MIR shifts `Shl`, `Shr`, `ShlUnchecked`, `ShrUnchecked` and calls to `core::intrinsics::unchecked_shl`/`unchecked_shr`, where LHS and RHS integer types may differ. Includes narrow 8/16-bit LHS with 32/128-bit RHS, 128-bit LHS with 8-bit RHS, signed and unsigned RHS, checked versus unchecked shifts, and both panic-abort and panic-unwind MIR revisions.
analysis.trigger: An unchecked shift has an RHS type different from the LHS type, especially when the RHS is wider than the LHS and must be truncated, or when a narrow-LHS `unchecked_shl`/`unchecked_shr` method is inlined and the old library code used to cast the RHS to the LHS type.
preconditions: MIR permits mismatched LHS and RHS integer types for shifts: "Shifts in MIR are all allowed to have mismatched LHS & RHS types."
The intrinsic signature has two type parameters: `unchecked_shl<T: Copy, U: Copy>(x: T, y: U) -> T` and the analogous `unchecked_shr`.
The builder shift helpers are homogeneous and are UB for out-of-range shift amounts, so checked shifts need masking and unchecked shifts need range facts instead.
The Inline regression test uses `//@ compile-flags: -Zmir-opt-level=2 -Zinline-mir` with `EMIT_MIR`.
pitfalls: Do not mask an unchecked shift: masking turns out-of-range UB inputs into defined results and removes the optimization freedom the unchecked operation is supposed to expose.
Do not omit RHS masking for checked `Shl`/`Shr`: the homogeneous builder shifts are UB out of range.

When truncating a wider unchecked RHS to the LHS width, preserve the in-range fact via assume or future `trunc nuw`; the codegen test expects the shift-width bound `icmp ult i32 %b, 16`, not the old truncation-range bound `65536`.

Signed RHS is still zero-extended when widened: the source comment says "We zero-extend even if the RHS is signed. So e.g. `(x: i32) << -1i8` will zero-extend the"; a negative RHS is UB for unchecked shifts.
Do not infer that a replacement pass is incorrect merely because MIR test files for bigger/smaller cases were deleted; the test comment explains the RHS type is no longer fixed in MIR.

LowerIntrinsics must preserve heterogeneous operands: the decoded new revision lowers `unchecked_shl::<i32, u32>(move _26, move _27)` directly to `ShlUnchecked(move _26, move _27)` with `_27: u32`, not to a casted homogeneous operand.
analysis.testStrategy: Extend `tests/mir-opt/lower_intrinsics.rs` with a `c: u32` parameter and CHECK that both `unchecked_shl::<i32,i32>`/`unchecked_shr::<i32,i32>` and `unchecked_shl::<i32,u32>`/`unchecked_shr::<i32,u32>` lower to `ShlUnchecked`/`ShrUnchecked` with the original RHS. In `tests/mir-opt/inline/unchecked_shifts.rs`, compile with `-Zmir-opt-level=2 -Zinline-mir` and EMIT_MIR, then check that inlined `u16.unchecked_shl(b: u32)` is `_0 = ShlUnchecked(_3, _4)` with `_4: u32`, with no `IntToInt` cast and no `assume`. At codegen level, cover same-type and mixed-type cases (`u128` LHS with `i8` RHS, `i128` LHS with `u8` RHS, `u8` LHS with `i128` RHS, `i8` LHS with `u128` RHS), verifying an assume appears only when the RHS is wider and its bound equals the LHS bit width (16 for u16/i16, 8 for u8/i8), while narrower RHS cases use `zext`/`zext nneg` with no assume. Compare both panic-abort and panic-unwind revisions. The const-eval test `tests/ui/consts/const-int-unchecked.rs` now uses `5_i16` so the intrinsic LHS is `i16` and overflow-shift const errors remain covered.
